notes.origin: Landfall Town (registry landfall_town, asset landfall_town): the building interiors behind the town's doors, one section per building. Its environment declares an enabled (dim) sun for the warm indoor key, so the look pass grades and paints it like the other sunlit interiors (crownwater_insides, ssarathi_insides). Written 2026-10-27 before the rooms' art landed: nothing here is measured yet. Measure in Forward+ against develop's frame once the shells, codex surfaces and furniture are published, and write the numbers down here.
notes.ground: deck_path 0: every room floor is a Walk_ deck from wall to wall (oak planks, limestone flags, cobalt-and-cream tiles, the smithy's packed earth), which LookGround would otherwise paint as road beige, as it did the tutorial courts (see bellwatch.json). At 0 each floor keeps its own colour and grain with the yard lift and no road edging. No deck_tint yet: solve it from develop's floor colour per renderer if the grade warms or greys the planks.
notes.sky: paint 0: the void between the rooms is meant black. With the painted sky on, the background beyond a cut-away wall would be lit sky and haze, as the Drowned Crown's and the archive's were. Measured 2026-10-27 (full_painted, Forward+): the void is (15, 15, 15), not black. That is the grade's toe (LookProfile.TOE_LIFT 0.06 lifts display black to 0.06), applied to the whole frame after the tone curve; the background is already black (environment backgroundColor #000000), so grade.background (a multiplier on it) cannot darken it, and no key in a region file turns the toe off. Default look: (0, 0, 0).
notes.props: keep_words cobalt, gilt, oak: the town's signature pieces (the cobalt glazed tiles and fittings, the palace's gilt, the oak furniture and beams) keep their chroma under the grade's warm key, matched as words of the material names the builder and the furniture kit write. decal_banner_, decal_rug_, decal_map_, decal_star_, decal_botanical_: the builder's decal materials (build_town_interiors.py names each `decal_<image>`: the eight peoples' banners, the tavern, runner and home rugs, the Landfall wall map, the star chart and the botanical prints; opaque or alpha-scissor, so LookFoliage.chroma_copy can draw them) keep their painted colours too: without them the saturation grade would grey the banners' heraldry and the rugs (the art role's warning, 2026-10-27; not yet measured in a render). keep_chroma_forward 1.15 follows the Drowned Crown's measurement for a warm-keyed interior (the default 1.45 went cyan there). decal_painting_, decal_book_, window_leaded (review 2026-10-27): the unlit-boat painting, Bettany's recipe book and the leaded glazing (window_leaded, window_leaded_tall) are kept too. Measured 2026-10-27 in Forward+ (full_painted against the default look, mean chroma max(rgb)-min(rgb) over each object in the rendered captures, work-output/lt-review/builder2): the painting 55 default, 30 painted before, 31 with its word; the book 130, 76, 80; the taproom glazing 75, 37, 38; the rug 175, 131; an oak table and chair 137, 110; the hall banners 96, 85. At keep_chroma_forward 1.45 they read 33, 89, 42, 137, 123 and 94, and the whole taproom frame 79 against 67 (default 96): the oak floor and furniture go back toward the default look. The rest of the painting's and the glass's loss is the grade's light (luminance and the cooler ambient), which keep_words do not touch. Left at 1.15: retuning every kept piece is a look call, not a fix.
